request: Project managers should be able to see the full history of engagement with a country before starting a new mission.
executive_summary: This release will enable project managers to view the complete history of engagement with selected countries while ensuring confidentiality through defined access controls. Features include access to engagement records, filtering options, and a clear presentation format. However, the specifics of permission granting and data verification processes require further decision-making.

core_commitments.text: Enable project managers to view the complete history of engagement with selected countries.
Ensure data on engagement history is presented in a clear, accessible format.

in_scope.text: Allow project managers to access engagement history records for any of the ~100 member countries.
in_scope.note: Project managers will access engagement history for all member countries to ensure comprehensive insights.

in_scope.text: Display engagement history that includes past projects, meeting notes, and communications related to the country.
Implement a filter option that allows project managers to search engagement history by date range or project type.
Ensure that only authorized project managers and regional coordinators, as defined by the organization’s access control policies, can access this engagement history data.
in_scope.note: Access will be restricted to authorized personnel as defined by the organization’s access control policies to protect sensitive data.

out_of_scope.text: Do not include a feature for editing engagement history records in this release.
Do not provide analytics or insights derived from engagement history data in this release.
Do not include integration with external databases or systems to fetch additional records.

assumptions.text: Project managers have the necessary permissions to view engagement history data, which is essential for them to access this feature.
assumptions.note: Assumes project managers have permissions to access data, but actual processes for permissions need clearer guidelines.

assumptions.text: All engagement history data is maintained accurately within the CRM, relying on previous data entry processes.
assumptions.note: Reliable data maintenance is assumed, but monitoring processes require further definition for quality assurance.

assumptions.text: Users have prior knowledge of how to navigate to the engagement history section in the CRM.

definitions.text: "Engagement history" means a chronological record of all documented interactions, meetings, projects, and communications related to a specific country stored within the CRM. This includes written communications such as emails and official reports, as well as notes from meetings. Access to engagement histories will vary based on their sensitivity, and more sensitive diplomatic records will have stricter access thresholds.
definitions.note: Definition of 'engagement history' has been refined to specify documented interactions, reducing ambiguity for users.

definitions.text: "Project managers" means individuals responsible for planning and executing missions who require full context regarding a country's past engagements to make informed decisions.

success_criteria.text: Achieve an 80% satisfaction rate from project managers regarding accessibility and clarity of engagement history within the first three months of release.

open_questions.question: What is the process for granting and revoking access permissions for project managers?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Clarifying permission processes is essential to mitigate risks of unauthorized access and ensure data protection.
options: Regularly review and update access permissions
Implement a formal access request and tracking system

proposer.text: The specifics of how access permissions are granted and maintained depend on organizational procedures and practices, which must be determined by the relevant authorities.

critic.text: How access permissions are granted and revoked depends on organizational procedures, which must be clarified.

open_questions.question: What system performance benchmarks are set to handle simultaneous requests for engagement histories?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Establishing performance benchmarks is crucial to ensure the system can support multiple project managers accessing data concurrently without failure.
options: Set user access limits during peak times

proposer.text: System performance benchmarks depend on organizational IT policies and infrastructure capabilities, which must be defined by the relevant technical teams.

critic.text: Performance benchmarks are determined by organizational IT policy, requiring further clarification.

open_questions.question: What processes are in place to regularly verify and update the accuracy of engagement history data?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Ensuring data accuracy is vital to prevent project managers from making decisions based on obsolete or incorrect information.
options: Schedule regular audits of engagement data
Develop a user feedback mechanism for data inaccuracies

proposer.text: The process for monitoring and verifying data quality must be established by the organization and is not solely determined by this feature release.

critic.text: Data monitoring processes are contingent on organizational policies, which need to be defined.

tension.summary: The main disagreement arose around the specifics of user access permissions and data quality assurance processes, both of which need to be defined by organizational policy. While the proposer recognized these concerns, the critic emphasized the risks posed by unclear protocols, necessitating further input from decision-makers.

proposer.worry: Ensuring the integrity and accuracy of sensitive data access in compliance with data protection standards.

critic.worry: Unclear processes for granting and revoking user permissions leave the system vulnerable to unauthorized access.
